name: Jezibah
title: Daughter of Job
summary: Jezibah (also known as Jemima) was the first of Job's three daughters born after his restoration. She is mentioned in the Book of Job as one of the most beautiful women in all the land. Together with her sisters, she received an inheritance among her brothers, which was unusual in ancient culture.

keyEvents.title: Job's Restoration
keyEvents.description: After God restored Job's wealth and health, Job had seven sons and three daughters, of whom Jezibah was the eldest daughter.

keyEvents.title: The Naming of Job's Daughters
keyEvents.description: Jezibah (Jemima) was named along with her sisters Keziah and Keren-Happuch. Their names were specifically mentioned, which was unusual in biblical genealogies.

keyEvents.title: Known for Her Beauty
keyEvents.description: Jezibah and her sisters were described as the most beautiful women in all the land, a sign of God's blessing upon Job.

keyEvents.title: Receiving an Inheritance Among Brothers
keyEvents.description: Job gave Jezibah and her sisters an inheritance among their brothers, which was very unusual in the society of that time and testified to Job's righteousness and generosity.

keyEvents.title: Part of Job's Blessed Old Age
keyEvents.description: Jozbekashah was part of the blessed period in Job's life when he lived an additional 140 years and saw four generations of his descendants.
